Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (including limited theatrical releases and streaming debuts). These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have received praise from critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling, time‑juggling saga that blends crime history with Scorsese’s signature storytelling. |
| 2 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh and Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Jennifer Lawrence | Sandler’s manic performance and the film’s relentless pacing make it a tense, almost claustrophobic thriller. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen | Though more courtroom drama, its political intrigue and sharp dialogue keep it in the crime‑thriller realm. |
| 4 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Hugh Grant, Michael Caine | Ritchie’s slick direction and witty script deliver a stylish, fast‑paced gangster caper. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen | A psychological thriller that examines how a single lie can spiral into a deadly conspiracy. |
| 6 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending tech paranoia with psychological terror. |
| 7 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A grim, atmospheric revenge story set in colonial Australia, blending crime with historical context. |
| 8 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval crime‑thriller that explores themes of justice, betrayal, and gender dynamics. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison as a metaphor for class warfare and human desperation. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending tech paranoia with psychological terror. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, or HBO Max.  
- **Blu‑ray/DVD**: For collectors, check your local retailer or online stores like Amazon or Best Buy.  
- **Special Editions**: Some films (e.g., *The Irishman*, *Uncut Gems*) have director’s cuts or extended editions that add extra depth.

Enjoy diving into the world of crime‑thrillers from 2020!
